info.title: Luca API
info.description:
The Luca API is the same surface the coach dashboard runs on. Every endpoint is
scoped to one coach, and every response is JSON.

## Authentication

Two credentials work. A Better Auth session cookie (`luca.session_token`) is
what the dashboard uses. An organization API key is what everything else uses.
send it as `x-api-key`, or as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

The two are not interchangeable. An API key only reaches the endpoints on the
published allowlist, and only with the scopes granted to that key. Endpoints
documented as session-only exist for the dashboard and return 403 to a key, no
matter its scopes. Each operation below lists which credentials it accepts.

Mint and revoke keys under **API keys**. `GET /api/capabilities` returns the
live list of what the calling credential can reach, which is cheaper than
probing.

## Workspaces

A user in more than one workspace picks one per request with
`x-luca-workspace-id` or `x-luca-workspace-slug`. Omit both and the request
resolves to the caller's default workspace.

## Errors

Every failure returns the same envelope, on every status:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "lead_not_found",
    "message": "lead not found",
    "requestId": "01JD…",
    "details": null
  }
}
```

Branch on `error.code`, never on `error.message`. The message is written for
a human and can change. Quote `requestId` in a support ticket and we can find
the exact request.

The statuses worth handling specifically:

| Status | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| 401 | No usable credential. |
| 402 | The workspace is unpaid, past due, or over its monthly message cap. |
| 403 | The plan tier or the key's scopes do not include this endpoint. |
| 409 | An idempotency key was reused with a different request body. |
| 429 | Rate limited. 120 requests per coach per minute, sliding window. |

## Idempotency

Mutations that create or launch something accept an `Idempotency-Key` header,
and some require it. A replayed key returns the original response with
`Idempotency-Replayed: true` instead of acting twice. Keys are held for 24
hours.

## Rate limits

120 requests per coach per minute, per endpoint, on a sliding window.

Every response under `/api` carries the quota policy. Every response that
reached the counter also carries the live state:

| Header | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `RateLimit-Policy` | The quota in effect, as `"default";q=120;w=60`. |
| `RateLimit` | What is left, as `"default";r=<remaining>;t=<seconds to reset>`. |
| `RateLimit-Limit` | The same quota as a bare integer. |
| `RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests left in the current window. |
| `RateLimit-Reset` | Seconds until the current window rolls over. |
| `Retry-After` | On a 429 only. Seconds to wait before retrying. |

`RateLimit-Policy` and `RateLimit` follow the IETF RateLimit header fields
draft. The `-Limit`/`-Remaining`/`-Reset` triple ships alongside them because
most SDKs still read that spelling. A request refused before it is attributed
to a coach, such as an unauthenticated 401, carries the policy without the live
state: there is no counter to report yet.

`RateLimit-Reset` and `Retry-After` count the seconds left in the current
window rather than a whole window, so a client that waits does not wait longer
than the limiter would have held it.

## Webhooks

Subscribe to events under **Webhooks** instead of polling.
`GET /api/webhook-subscriptions/signature-guide` returns the signing scheme
and a verification example.

## Versioning

This is version 1 of the API. Every response carries `Luca-API-Version: 1`, and
`info.version` in this document is the spec revision within that major version.

Inside a major version we only make additive changes: new endpoints, new
optional request fields, new properties on an existing response. Treat unknown
response properties as forgiving — do not fail a parse because a field you have
not seen appeared. Anything that would break a correct client (removing a field,
narrowing a type, changing a status code, tightening validation) ships as a new
major version on a new path prefix, and version 1 keeps serving.

Send `Luca-API-Version: 1` on a request to assert the major version you built
against. Naming any other major version is refused with 400
`unsupported_api_version`, rather than served by a version that does not match
what the client expects. Omit the header and the request is served by version 1.

## Deprecation

A retiring endpoint is announced on the endpoint itself, so a running
integration finds out without anyone reading a changelog. Two response headers
carry it:

| Header | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Deprecation` | An HTTP date. The endpoint is deprecated as of this date and still works. |
| `Sunset` | An HTTP date. After this the endpoint stops answering. |

`Deprecation` follows RFC 9745, `Sunset` follows RFC 8594. A deprecated
operation is also marked `deprecated: true` in this document, so a generated
client can surface it at build time. Watch for both headers and alert on them.

tags.name: Capabilities
tags.description: What the calling credential can actually reach. Read this first. It answers the scope and plan-tier question for the current key without probing every endpoint for a 403.

tags.name: Debug
tags.description: Inspect how a recent inbound message moved through the pipeline. Diagnostic only, and session-only.

tags.name: Leads
tags.description: People who messaged the coach. A lead carries the score, stage, consents, notes, and custom fields, and is the anchor every conversation, booking, and campaign enrollment hangs off. Bulk import lives here too. Preview first, then apply.

tags.name: Conversations
tags.description: Message threads with a lead, across every connected channel. Sending here writes to the real channel, so an auto-send-disabled workspace should queue a draft through the review queue instead.

tags.name: Review queue
tags.description: The human approval step. Auto-send is off by default, so every AI-drafted reply lands here to be approved, rejected, or restored. `explain` returns why Luca wrote what it wrote.

tags.name: Memory
tags.description: Durable facts Luca carries between conversations about a coach or a lead. Editing memory changes future drafts.

tags.name: Bookings
tags.description: Scheduled calls and their outcomes. Covers the booking record, the pre-call brief, guest links, and the outcome each call is closed with.

tags.name: Booking types
tags.description: The call types a coach offers: duration, attendees, and the schedule each one is bookable on.

tags.name: Booking providers
tags.description: Connections to Calendly, Cal.com, iClosed, GoHighLevel, or a manual link, plus the calendars and availability they expose.

tags.name: Call events
tags.description: What happened on a call: recording-derived summaries, feedback, CRM push, and outcome corrections.

tags.name: Campaigns
tags.description: Multi-step outreach a lead is enrolled into. Draft, simulate against real provider capabilities, publish, then read per-enrollment timelines.

tags.name: Broadcasts
tags.description: One message to a segment. Preview and approve before launch. You can pause a launched broadcast, but sent messages don't come back.

tags.name: Cadences
tags.description: Silent-lead rescue. Starts the follow-up sequence for leads who went quiet.

tags.name: A/B tests
tags.description: Split tests over drafted replies and objection handling. A winner can be adopted into the live playbook.

tags.name: Voice
tags.description: The voice fingerprint: the corpus of the coach's own writing that every draft is matched against. This is a visible product surface, not backend plumbing: changing it visibly changes how Luca sounds.

tags.name: Knowledge
tags.description: Source material Luca can cite: offers, program details, and FAQs. Suggestions are Luca proposing new knowledge it inferred; they take effect only once approved.

tags.name: Teach Luca
tags.description: The question-and-answer loop that fills gaps in what Luca knows about the coach's business.

tags.name: Objections
tags.description: The objection playbook: recurring objections and the responses that work on them.

tags.name: Learning
tags.description: What Luca has learned from outcomes: proposed prompt changes awaiting review, and how each sales framework is performing.

tags.name: Copilot
tags.description: Ask Luca, the in-app chat agent. Chats, streaming tokens, and the confirm/discard step for actions it proposes taking.

tags.name: Analytics
tags.description: The measurement surface: funnel, revenue, forecast, speed-to-lead, objections, call intelligence, content attribution, and cross-workspace benchmarks. Benchmarks require explicit consent.

tags.name: Insights
tags.description: The proactive feed. Luca surfaces something worth acting on, and the coach reads, acts on, or dismisses it.

tags.name: Reports
tags.description: Prepared rollups: the morning report and the scorecard.

tags.name: Audit log
tags.description: Who changed what, and when. Every mutation that touches coach-visible state writes a row here.

tags.name: Channels
tags.description: Telegram, Instagram, Messenger, and WhatsApp connections.

tags.name: Integrations
tags.description: The connector catalog and the integration event stream.

tags.name: CRM
tags.description: CRM connections: OAuth, field mappings, schema discovery, sync runs, and connection health.

tags.name: OAuth connections
tags.description: Third-party authorizations granted to this workspace, and revoking them.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Outbound event delivery. Subscribe, inspect deliveries, replay a failed one, and verify signatures with the signing guide.

tags.name: Coach profile
tags.description: The coach record and how they sell: niche, sales framework, objection playbook, and post-call CRM behavior.

tags.name: Onboarding
tags.description: First-time setup: profile, channel connection, voice corpus seeding, and preferences.

tags.name: Workspaces
tags.description: List the workspaces the signed-in user belongs to, and create or recover their personal workspace.

tags.name: First run
tags.description: The activation checklist a new coach works through, and the value it has produced so far.

tags.name: Settings
tags.description: Workspace behavior toggles: auto-send, multi-part drafts, the tool belt, and voice settings.

tags.name: Team members
tags.description: Invite people to a workspace, change their role and extra permissions, remove them, and accept or decline an invitation.

tags.name: Privacy
tags.description: The signed-in user's own choices: terms acceptance and the account advertising choice. API keys cannot call these routes.

tags.name: API keys
tags.description: Create, scope, and revoke the organization API keys this API accepts. A key is shown once, at creation.

tags.name: Mobile
tags.description: Push device registration and notification preferences. Notifications carry routing metadata only, never message or draft text.

tags.name: Account safety
tags.description: The health of a workspace's channel connections against platform rate limits and behavioral limits.

tags.name: Billing
tags.description: Subscription state, Stripe Checkout, the customer portal, and message top-up packs.

tags.name: Usage
tags.description: Month-to-date consumption against the plan's message pool and model budget.

tags.name: Cancellation
tags.description: The cancel flow: context, retention offer, survey, confirmation, and reactivation.

ErrorEnvelope.title: ErrorEnvelope
ErrorEnvelope.description: The response body of every failure, on every status. Branch on `error.code`; `error.message` is written for a human and can change. Quote `error.requestId` in a support ticket.

LucaApiVersion.name: Luca-API-Version
LucaApiVersion.description: The major version of the API this client was built against. Omit it and the request is served by the current major version. Any other value is refused with 400 `unsupported_api_version`.

sessionCookie.name: luca.session_token
sessionCookie.description: Better Auth session cookie, set by signing in to the dashboard. Shared across app and API on a common parent domain. Every endpoint accepts it.

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Organization API key. Reaches only allowlisted endpoints, and only within the scopes granted to the key.

bearerAuth.description: The same organization API key sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, for clients that cannot set a custom header.

get.summary: List the coach's A/B tests
get.description:
Every test this coach has, newest first. Filter by status. Variant config comes back as stored, since its shape depends on what the test compares.

**API key scopes:** `learning:read`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Return only records in this status.

post.summary: Create a sales-framework A/B test
post.description:
Sets up a head-to-head between two sales frameworks. It starts as a draft unless you pass `start: true`. Only one framework test can run at a time. A framework test matches every lead, so a second one would split the same traffic twice and starve both. You'll get a 409 if one's already running.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

post.summary: Create an objection-strategy A/B test
post.description:
Compares two ways of answering one objection bucket, like price or timing. It starts as a draft unless you pass `start: true`. Buckets are independent, so tests on different buckets run side by side. A second test on the same bucket returns 409.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

get.summary: Get an A/B test with per-variant stats
get.description:
One test with its per-variant numbers: how many leads each arm saw, and how each is doing against the success metric.

**API key scopes:** `learning:read`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the A/B test this operation targets.

post.summary: Start an A/B test
post.description:
Puts a draft or paused test into live lead assignment. Any other status returns 409, and so does a conflicting test that's already running.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the A/B test this operation targets.

post.summary: Pause an A/B test
post.description:
Stops assigning new leads and keeps the results so far. Only a running test can pause. Start it again later and it picks up where it left off.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the A/B test this operation targets.

post.summary: Stop an A/B test
post.description:
Ends the test for good and records the winner. A completed test can't go back to running, so a finished result can't be reopened and re-decided.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the A/B test this operation targets.

post.summary: Adopt a completed A/B test's winning framework
post.description:
Switches the coach onto the winning framework. It's a no-op that returns `adopted: false` unless the test is completed and its winner points at a real framework.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the A/B test this operation targets.

get.summary: Get the coach's framework objection-performance snapshot
get.description:
Win rate by objection bucket for the sales framework the coach has configured right now, over a rolling window (30 days by default, 1 to 90 allowed). These numbers are correlational, so read them as a signal and not as proof.

**API key scopes:** `learning:read`.

parameters.name: windowDays
parameters.description: Size of the lookback window, in days.

get.summary: List the coach's learning proposals
get.description:
What the A/B tests have learned and are proposing you act on. It defaults to the ab_test.* event types over the last 30 days, newest first, and leaves out dismissed proposals unless you pass `activeOnly=false`.

**API key scopes:** `learning:read`.

parameters.name: eventTypes
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of event types to include.

parameters.name: activeOnly
parameters.description: Return only records that are still active.

post.summary: Dismiss a learning proposal
post.description:
Dismisses one proposal so it drops out of the default list. You'll get a 404 when the analytics event doesn't exist, or belongs to another coach.

**API key scopes:** `learning:write`. You also need an `Idempotency-Key` header.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the learning proposal this operation targets.

get.summary: Read the current coach profile
get.description:
The dashboard's first read on every page load. It returns identity, timezone and business hours, the tone slider, feature flags like auto-send, the plan tier and status, and whether onboarding is finished. Integrations report connection status only. Provider tokens never leave the server.

**API key scopes:** `coach:read`.

patch.summary: Update name, timezone, business hours, or tone slider
patch.description:
Updates only the fields you send. Sending `businessHours` sets its `tz` as the coach's timezone too, so the two can't ever disagree.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

get.summary: Read the coach's niche & offer profile
get.description:
The coach-authored context the drafter compiles into its prompt: niche, audience, offer, pricing, and FAQs. It's what lets a reply answer an offer question instead of guessing. The response includes `profileUpdatedAt` for full-form compare-and-set saves. You get `null` before the coach has filled it in.

**API key scopes:** `coach:read`.

put.summary: Replace the coach's niche & offer profile
put.description:
A full replacement, not a patch. Send the whole profile back, or the missing fields get cleared. The sales framework has its own endpoint, so the two editors can't overwrite each other. Include `expectedUpdatedAt` from GET when saving a previously loaded form; the server returns 409 if another write landed first.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

get.summary: Read the coach's canonical niche (benchmark cohort key)
get.description:
The fixed-taxonomy cohort key that decides which coaches this one is benchmarked against. It's not the free-text `niche` on the niche and offer profile, which describes the business instead of naming a cohort.

**API key scopes:** `coach:read`.

put.summary: Set the coach's canonical niche (benchmark cohort key)
put.description:
Sets the benchmark cohort key. Send `null` to leave the cohort, which drops the coach out of niche benchmark comparisons.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

put.summary: Set (or clear) the coach's sales framework
put.description:
Sets the sales methodology the drafter follows, either a built-in framework or a custom one. Send `null` to clear it. It writes only the framework slice of the profile, so it never clobbers an edit made on the business tab.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

post.summary: Parse a coach's free-text sales-process description into a candidate custom framework for preview
post.description:
Turns a coach's description of how they sell into candidate framework stages you can preview. Nothing is saved. The coach confirms in the UI, which then calls the sell-framework endpoint. If fewer than two usable stages come back you get `ok: false` with a message, and the coach keeps their current framework.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

get.summary: Read the coach's objection playbook
get.description:
How the drafter should handle each objection bucket (price, timing, trust, fit, authority, smokescreen), plus the social proof it may cite. You get `null` before the coach has written one.

**API key scopes:** `coach:read`.

put.description:
Replaces the coach-written half of the playbook: overrides and social proof sources. Patterns learned from imported conversations are kept, so saving this form can't wipe an import that landed after the page loaded. You'll get a 409 if the playbook changed underneath you.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

get.summary: Read the coach's post-call preferences
get.description:
What happens after a call ends: reminders, automatic summaries, CRM sync, and how much detail to include. Unset fields come back as their defaults instead of nulls.

**API key scopes:** `coach:read`.

put.description:
Replaces the post-call preferences. The response is the resolved settings, defaults included, so it matches what the pipeline will actually read.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

get.summary: Read the coach's post-call CRM field mapping
get.description:
Which Luca call fields land in which CRM fields, plus a `connected` flag telling you whether a CRM is hooked up at all. You can read the mapping before connecting a CRM.

**API key scopes:** `coach:read`.

put.summary: Update the coach's post-call CRM field mapping
put.description:
Saves the field mapping. You'll get a 404 with `crm_not_connected` when there's no CRM to map into, so connect one first.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

get.summary: Read the coach's post-call CRM deal-stage sync config
get.description:
Which CRM deal stage each call outcome should move a deal to, plus a `connected` flag for whether a CRM is hooked up.

**API key scopes:** `coach:read`.

put.summary: Update the coach's post-call CRM deal-stage sync config
put.description:
Saves the outcome-to-deal-stage mapping. You'll get a 404 with `crm_not_connected` when no CRM is connected.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

get.summary: Post-call intelligence: show rate, ratings, day-of-week, surprises
get.description:
Post-call patterns over a window: show rate, ratings, day-of-week effects, and the surprises worth a look.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Start of the time range, inclusive.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: End of the time range, exclusive.

get.summary: Recent post-call summaries, most recent first
get.description:
The latest post-call summaries, most recent first.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of items to return on this page.

get.summary: Read-only rollup of agent-improvement signals from call feedback
get.description:
What call feedback suggests about improving the agents. It's read-only. Adopting a change happens under Learning.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Start of the time range, inclusive.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: End of the time range, exclusive.

get.summary: Aggregate CRM-sync health for the coach's call summaries
get.description:
How reliably call summaries are reaching the CRM, totalled across connections.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

get.summary: Read safe PostHog analytics context
get.description:
The analytics context the app hands to PostHog. It holds identifiers that are safe to send to a third party, and nothing tenant-sensitive.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

get.summary: Read the coach's lead funnel for a period
get.description:
Lead counts at each funnel stage over a period. It's the shape most of the other analytics endpoints drill into.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Reporting window the figures cover.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: Return only records on this messaging channel.

get.summary: Read the coach's AI-attributed revenue and plan ROI for a period
get.description:
Revenue attributed to Luca over a period, sat next to what the plan costs, as a return figure.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Reporting window the figures cover.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: Return only records on this messaging channel.

get.summary: Read fast-vs-slow first-reply booking-rate impact for a period
get.description:
Booking rate on fast first replies against slow ones. It's the argument for keeping the review queue short.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Reporting window the figures cover.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: Return only records on this messaging channel.

get.summary: Read a point-in-time pipeline revenue forecast
get.description:
A pipeline revenue forecast built from the leads and bookings that are open right now. It's a snapshot, not a series.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

get.summary: Read ghosted-lead counts, recovery rate, and top conversation killers
get.description:
How many leads went quiet, how many came back, and the conversation patterns that usually show up right before a ghost.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Reporting window the figures cover.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: Return only records on this messaging channel.

get.summary: Read draft approval/edit/rejection rates and auto-send gate state
get.description:
How often the coach approves, edits, or rejects drafts, and where that leaves the auto-send gate. This is the number that decides whether auto-send can go on at all.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Reporting window the figures cover.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: Return only records on this messaging channel.

get.summary: Read the coach's weekly metrics as a trend series
get.description:
The stored weekly rollup as a series. It takes a `weeks` count instead of a date window, because the table behind it is already bucketed by week.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

parameters.name: weeks
parameters.description: Number of weeks the report covers.

get.summary: Score one of the coach's leads against the trained predictive lead-scoring model
get.description:
Scores one lead against the trained model and shows which factors moved the score.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

parameters.name: leadId
parameters.description: Identifier of the lead this operation targets.

get.summary: Read the category breakdown of automatic per-lead loss analyses for a period
get.description:
Why leads were lost over a period, grouped into categories from the automatic per-lead loss analyses.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Reporting window the figures cover.

get.summary: Read the coach's active prescriptive recommendations for a week
get.description:
The recommendations active for a week: what to change, and the evidence behind each one.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

parameters.name: weekStart
parameters.description: The Monday of the week to report on.

parameters.name: includeDismissed
parameters.description: Include records the coach has dismissed.

get.summary: Read the per-content rollup (leads, qualified, booked, revenue) of attributed touches for a period
get.description:
Leads, qualified leads, bookings, and revenue traced back to each piece of content over a period.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Reporting window the figures cover.

get.summary: Read the per-post rollup (reach, engagement, leads, bookings, revenue) for a period
get.description:
Reach, engagement, and what came of it, post by post, over a period.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Reporting window the figures cover.

get.summary: Read the per-topic weekly rollup (engagement, leads, bookings, revenue) for a week
get.description:
The same rollup grouped by topic instead of by post, for one week.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

parameters.name: weekStart
parameters.description: The Monday of the week to report on.

get.summary: Read the coach's cross-coach benchmark percentiles, if any
get.description:
Where this coach sits against comparable coaches, as percentiles. It stays empty until the coach opts in and there are enough peers to compare against.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

get.summary: Read the coach's cross-coach benchmark opt-in state
get.description:
Whether the coach has opted into cross-coach benchmarking.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

put.summary: Set the coach's cross-coach benchmark opt-in state
put.description:
Turns benchmarking on or off. Opting out also stops this coach's data feeding anyone else's benchmarks.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

get.summary: Read the objection-bucket rollup over the review queue's signals
get.description:
The objections leads raised, bucketed by type, from the signals the review queue captured.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

parameters.name: period

get.description:
The individual conversations behind one objection bucket, so you can trace a rollup number back to real messages.

**API key scopes:** `analytics:read`.

get.summary: List connected knowledge sources
get.description:
The content sources the coach has connected, like Notion, Google Docs, a public website, or an Instagram bio, with the sync state of each one.

**API key scopes:** `knowledge:read`.

post.summary: Connect a new knowledge source
post.description:
Registers a content source for the extraction pipeline to read. Sources start in `connected` status. The sync that produces suggestions runs on its own schedule, or on demand through the sync route.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

delete.description:
Deletes the source row. Its suggestions go with it through a foreign-key cascade, so anything still pending disappears. Values the coach already approved stay in the profile, because approval copies them there.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the knowledge source this operation targets.

post.summary: Request an on-demand sync for a knowledge source
post.description:
Queues a re-read of the source now, instead of waiting for the next scheduled sync. It returns as soon as the job is queued.

**API key scopes:** `knowledge:write`. You also need an `Idempotency-Key` header.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the knowledge source this operation targets.

get.summary: List profile suggestions produced from knowledge sources
get.description:
Field-level profile changes pulled out of connected sources, filterable by status. Nothing here has touched the coach profile yet.

**API key scopes:** `knowledge:read`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Return only records in this status.

post.summary: Approve a profile suggestion and apply it to the coach profile
post.description:
The human approval that lets ingested content reach the profile. It writes through the same path a direct profile edit uses, and re-checks the field against the allowlist instead of trusting the stored row. Approving a suggestion that's already resolved returns 409.

**API key scopes:** `knowledge:write`. You also need an `Idempotency-Key` header.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the suggestion this operation targets.

post.summary: Reject a profile suggestion
post.description:
Turns the suggestion down and leaves the profile alone. Rejecting one that's already resolved returns 409.

**API key scopes:** `knowledge:write`. You also need an `Idempotency-Key` header.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the suggestion this operation targets.

get.summary: List recent webhook events of one type
get.description:
Newest-first canonical events, in exactly the shape we deliver them (unique top-level id). If the workspace has no events of that type yet, you get the documented sample payload instead. This is the polling source platform integrations use for sample data, such as Zapier's performList.

**API key scopes:** `webhooks:read`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Return only records of this type.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of items to return on this page.

get.summary: List webhook subscriptions
get.description:
The workspace's webhook subscriptions, with the event types each one receives.

**API key scopes:** `webhooks:read`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of items to return on this page.

parameters.description: Include a live provider health check. It costs an extra upstream call.

post.summary: Create webhook subscription
post.description:
Subscribes a URL to one or more event types. The signing secret comes back once, so store it now. We check the target URL first and refuse private and loopback addresses.

**API key scopes:** `webhooks:write`.

patch.description:
Changes the target URL, the event types, or the active flag. We re-check the URL on every change.

**API key scopes:** `webhooks:write`. You also need an `Idempotency-Key` header.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the webhook subscription this operation targets.

delete.description:
A terminal soft delete. Delivery history stays queryable, the subscription stops receiving events, and repeating the delete still succeeds. That's the shape platform unsubscribe hooks like Zapier and Make expect.

**API key scopes:** `webhooks:write`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the webhook subscription this operation targets.

post.summary: Queue a canonical test webhook event
post.description:
Queues a canonical test event to your subscriptions, so you can prove a receiver works without waiting for real activity.

**API key scopes:** `webhooks:write`. You also need an `Idempotency-Key` header.

get.summary: List webhook deliveries
get.description:
Delivery attempts with the response status of each one. Start here when you're working out what failed and why.

**API key scopes:** `webhooks:read`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of items to return on this page.

get.summary: Describe webhook HMAC verification
get.description:
The HMAC scheme we sign with, the headers to read, and an example that verifies a payload. Read this before you write a receiver.

**API key scopes:** `webhooks:read`.

post.summary: Replay one webhook delivery
post.description:
Re-sends one delivery to the subscription it was meant for.

**API key scopes:** `webhooks:write`. You also need an `Idempotency-Key` header.

parameters.name: deliveryId
parameters.description: Identifier of the delivery this operation targets.

post.summary: Replay one event to one or all matching active subscriptions
post.description:
Re-sends one event, either to a single subscription or to every active one that matches its type. Only events still inside the retention window can be replayed.

**API key scopes:** `webhooks:write`. You also need an `Idempotency-Key` header.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: Identifier of the event this operation targets.

post.summary: Bulk replay events by type and time range
post.description:
Re-sends every event of a type inside a time range. This can be a big burst, so make sure the receiver is idempotent before you call it.

**API key scopes:** `webhooks:write`. You also need an `Idempotency-Key` header.

get.summary: List coach long-term memories

Filter what Luca remembers by scope, lead, state, source, trust level, or a free-text search. Archived memories are left out unless you ask for them.

patch.description:
Edit a memory's content, confidence, metadata, reason, or evidence. Set `disputed` to flag a fact as wrong, `restore` to bring an archived one back, or `preferred` to make it win over conflicting memories. Provenance and trust fields belong to the server and can't be set here.

Archives the memory instead of erasing it, so Luca stops using the fact while the record and its provenance survive. Reverse it with a `restore` patch.

parameters.name: expectedUpdatedAt
parameters.description: The `expectedUpdatedAt` this operation targets.

post.summary: Archive or restore multiple long-term memories
post.description:
Archive or restore a list of memory ids in one call. The response says which ids were affected, so ids that no longer exist are just left out.

**API key scopes:** `memory:write`. You also need an `Idempotency-Key` header.

get.summary: List the coach's connected agents (active OAuth connections)
get.description:
Every agent the coach has authorized over OAuth, newest first, with the scopes it holds and when it was last used. Revoked connections are left out.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

delete.summary: Revoke a connected agent and kill its vended API key
delete.description:
The kill switch for a connected agent. It marks the connection revoked and deletes the API key we vended it, so public API access stops right away. It also drops the stored consent, so the next authorize shows a real consent screen, and clears the refresh and access tokens.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the OAuth connection this operation targets.

post.summary: Register or update a mobile push device
post.description:
Records the Expo push token for this device against the signed-in user. Registering the same device twice updates the existing row instead of adding another, so it's safe to send a token refresh on every launch. This one needs a user session, and an API key is rejected.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

delete.description:
Turns push off for one device without deleting its history. A user can only disable their own devices.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the device this operation targets.

get.summary: Read mobile notification preferences
get.description:
Which push notifications this user wants on their phone, plus quiet hours. This one needs a user session, and an API key is rejected.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

patch.description:
Updates only the preference fields you send. Push payloads carry routing metadata and nothing else, so changing these never changes how much lead content leaves the server.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

get.summary: List booking provider capabilities and health
get.description:
Every booking provider Luca supports, what each one can do, and whether this coach's connection is healthy or needs reconnecting. The bookings settings screen renders from this.

**API key scopes:** `bookings:read`.

post.summary: Connect or reconnect a booking provider
post.description:
Stores the provider credentials, encrypted, and mints a webhook secret the provider signs its callbacks with. The secret comes back once, in this response, so capture it here. Calling it again on a connected provider replaces the credentials.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: The provider this operation targets.

delete.description:
Removes the credentials and cleans up what the provider holds on its side, like registered webhooks. If that remote cleanup fails we keep the connection and return 502, so you're never left with a half-torn-down provider.

**Session-only.** This endpoint isn't on the API-key allowlist. An organization API key gets a 403 here, whatever scopes it holds.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: The provider this operation targets.

get.summary: List booking provider event types and calendars

get.description:
The call types the coach offers when Luca books through its own scheduler instead of an external provider.

post.description:
Defines a bookable call: how long it runs, where it happens, and how it looks to the lead. Give it a schedule next. A booking type with no schedule offers no slots.

**API key scopes:** `bookings:write`. You also need an `Idempotency-Key` header.

patch.description:
Updates only the fields you send. Sending `location` replaces the whole location, because its shape depends on the type.

**API key scopes:** `bookings:write`. You also need an `Idempotency-Key` header.

The weekly rules and date-specific overrides that decide which slots this booking type offers.

parameters.name: id

get.description:
Where the sale stands on this booking: current status, the loss reason if there is one, and the version you'll send back when you correct it.

parameters.description: Identifier of the booking this operation targets.

post.description:
Records what the call was worth: won, lost with a reason, or still open. Send an `Idempotency-Key` so a retried submit can't write twice. To correct an outcome, send the `expectedVersion` you read. A stale version returns 409 with the current one, so you can re-read and try again.

parameters.description: Key that makes this mutation safe to retry. Replaying a key returns the original response with `Idempotency-Replayed: true` instead of acting twice.

get.summary: Read append-only sales outcome history for a booking
get.description:
Every outcome ever recorded on this booking, in order. The log only appends, so a correction adds an event instead of rewriting the old one. That's what tells you who changed the outcome, and when.

**API key scopes:** `bookings:read`.

parameters.name: id

get.summary: List active sales and booking outcome reasons
get.description:
The reasons a coach picks from when a sale is lost, or a call gets cancelled or no-showed. Covers the built-in reasons and the workspace's own. Archived ones don't appear.

**API key scopes:** `bookings:read`.

parameters.name: kind

post.summary: Create a workspace-specific sales or booking reason
post.description:
Adds a reason in the workspace's own wording, optionally scoped to one booking type. A code that's already taken returns 409.

**API key scopes:** `bookings:write`. You also need an `Idempotency-Key` header.

patch.summary: Rename, order, activate, or archive a workspace reason
patch.description:
Renames a reason, reorders it, or archives it with `active: false`. Archiving only hides it from the picker. Outcomes already recorded against it keep it.

post.summary: Create revocable guest management links
post.description:
Mints revocable links that let a guest manage this booking without an account. It isn't available for providers that run their own rescheduling flow.

**API key scopes:** `bookings:write`. You also need an `Idempotency-Key` header.

parameters.name: id

**API key scopes:** `bookings:write`. You also need an `Idempotency-Key` header.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the booking this operation targets.

get.summary: List bookings that need a lifecycle decision
get.description:
Bookings where our record and the provider's disagree: a failed write-back, a suspected duplicate, a cancellation we never saw.

post.description:

Bookings whose call time has passed with no outcome recorded. It's the work list for closing the loop on revenue attribution.

get.summary: List call events awaiting the coach's outcome/feedback
get.description:
The post-call queue: calls whose time has passed that still need the coach to say what happened. This drives the outcome prompt in the dashboard.

get.description:
One call event with its outcome, rating, summary, and CRM sync state.

get.summary: List every call event for a lead (call history), oldest call first
get.description:
The full call history for one lead, oldest first, so a second or third call reads in sequence.

**API key scopes:** `call_events:read`.

parameters.name: leadId
parameters.description: Identifier of the lead this operation targets.

post.description:
Creates a call event for a booking that predates automatic creation, then queues its summary. It only works on calls whose time has passed. A future booking returns 409, because there's no conversation to summarize and the summary would be made up. Safe to call twice: an existing call event comes back as is.

post.summary: Report a call's outcome, rating, and structured feedback

The coach's report on how the call went. A `completed` or `no_show` outcome also records booking attendance, and a completed call queues its summary. Resubmitting the identical form is deduped. A correction, like a fixed rating or an added note, runs the learning loop again.

post.summary: Generate (or regenerate) the AI summary for a call event

**API key scopes:** `call_events:write`. You also need an `Idempotency-Key` header.

parameters.name: id

put.summary: Edit a call summary before it is pushed to the CRM
